comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers fully support claims C1, C34-C43 regarding starvation duration determining memory type. Both cite Figure 1 data showing differential memory formation across starvation durations and genotypes with appropriate statistical comparisons.

Strong agreement. Both support claims C46-C57 on memory type characterization using cold-shock sensitivity. OpenEval emphasizes systematic cold-shock experiments and dopaminergic neuron blocking (C51-C52), while peer reviewers accept the meticulously designed experiments without methodological critique.

Strong agreement on octopamine's inhibitory role. Both support claims C4, C58-C61 showing octopamine negatively regulates appetitive memory. OpenEval notes bidirectional pharmacological effects in Figure 3A-B. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm octopamine's suppressive effect on learning and memory.

Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates claims C62-C65 on octopamine affecting food evaluation, finding C64-C65 speculative. Peer R3 addresses broader octopamine claims (C4, C58-C65) and fully supports the negative regulatory role without distinguishing mechanistic speculation.

Agreement on glycogen measurements. OpenEval supports claims C66-C68 showing elevated glycogen in mutants (Figure 4A) with modest sample sizes but significant effects. Peer R5 addresses broader glycogen findings (C2, C66-C89) and affirms glycogen's crucial role without methodological concerns.

Strong agreement on food choice and glycogen correlation. OpenEval supports claims C69-C77 on food preference experiments and nutrient sensing. Peer R5 encompasses these claims within broader glycogen findings (C2, C66-C89) and accepts tissue-specific RNAi manipulations without critique.

Agreement on tissue-specific glycogen manipulation. OpenEval supports claims C78-C89 on RNAi experiments in muscles and fat body. Peer R5 includes these claims (C82-C89) in broader glycogen evaluation and accepts the coordinated signaling interpretation between tissues.

Agreement on glycogen reduction rescuing STM. OpenEval supports claims C90-C92 showing combined glycogen reduction restores STM in mutants (Figure 6A). Peer R4 addresses these claims within broader reinterpretation of octopamine's role (C5-C6, C90-C99), accepting the energy status mechanism.

Agreement on reward specificity. OpenEval supports claims C93-C95 showing memory deficit is specific to sucrose rewards. Peer R4 includes C95 in broader evaluation of octopamine reinterpretation, accepting that octopamine gates memory formation based on energy status.

Agreement on mating effects and energy status. OpenEval supports claims C96-C99 on virgin vs. mated females showing energy status determines reward valuation. Peer R4 addresses these claims as part of octopamine reinterpretation, confirming energy gating mechanism.

Strong agreement on insulin signaling mechanism. OpenEval supports claims C100-C108 on InR expression and manipulation rescuing STM. Peer R6 addresses overlapping claims (C3, C102-C112, C140) and explicitly supports the insulin receptor sensing mechanism in octopaminergic neurons.

Agreement on integrative model. OpenEval supports claims C109-C112 as well-grounded inferential model integrating glycogen, insulin, and octopamine findings. Peer R6 includes these claims and confirms the proposed mechanism is well-supported by data.

Agreement on food intake findings. OpenEval supports claims C113-C118 on overconsumption after prolonged starvation despite elevated glycogen. Peer R7 addresses these claims within broader food intake evaluation (C113-C121, C149-C151) and accepts the findings without question.

Agreement on InR blockade rescuing feeding. OpenEval supports claims C119-C121 showing InR blockade rescues feeding deficit in mutants. Peer R7 includes these claims and accepts the parallel between memory and food intake regulation through insulin signaling.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate claims C7-C8, C153-C154 as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval notes the causal relationship between memory stability and overconsumption is not directly tested. Peer R8 notes these speculative claims about broader implications are not explicitly evaluated.

Agreement on mechanistic interpretation. OpenEval supports claims C125-C129 on LTM formation and dopaminergic involvement. Peer R9 addresses these claims within broader integrative interpretation (C125-C158) and confirms the mechanistic framework is well-supported.

Agreement on octopamine reinterpretation. OpenEval supports claims C134-C135, C137 on reinterpreting octopamine's role as energy status sensor. Peer R9 includes these claims and explicitly supports this clarification of octopamine's function in memory formation.

Perfect agreement. Both support claims C143-C144, C147 on inter-tissue communication through glycogen signaling. OpenEval notes these are reasonable inferences from tissue-specific experiments. Peer R10 accepts the logic connecting tissue requirements to communication without challenge.

Agreement on energy status affecting reward processing. OpenEval supports claims C140, C149-C151 on InR blockade effects and modest feeding increases. Peer R7 includes these claims and accepts the integrated findings across multiple figures.

Agreement on summary conclusions with partial speculation. OpenEval supports claims C155-C160 as well-supported synthesis with some speculative elements (C159-C160). Peer R9 addresses C155-C158 and confirms overall take-home message is clear and supported, but does not evaluate C159-C160 specifically.

Agreement on uncertainty about evolutionary conservation. OpenEval notes claim C160 on octopamine-noradrenaline conservation is speculative but grounded in functional relationships. Peer R11 does not specifically evaluate this speculation about conservation beyond Drosophila, rating it as uncertain.
